source_text: Descending properties of morphisms in the fppf topology

<STRUCT_0001>
In this section we find some properties of morphisms of algebraic spaces
for which we could not (yet) show they are local on the base in
the fpqc topology which, however, are local on the base
in the fppf topology.

The property <MATH_0001>``<MATH_0002> is an immersion''
is fppf local on the base.

Let <MATH_0001> be a morphism of algebraic spaces.
Let <MATH_0002> be an fppf covering of <MATH_0003>.
Let <MATH_0004> be the base change of <MATH_0005>.

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
If <MATH_0006> is an immersion, then each <MATH_0007> is an immersion by
Spaces, Lemma <REF_0001>.
This proves the direct implication in
Definition <REF_0002>.

<STRUCT_0003><STRUCT_0004>
Conversely, assume each <MATH_0008> is an immersion. By
Morphisms of Spaces,
Lemma <REF_0003>
this implies each <MATH_0009> is separated. By
Morphisms of Spaces,
Lemma <REF_0004>
this implies each <MATH_0010> is locally quasi-finite.
Hence we see that <MATH_0011> is locally quasi-finite and separated, by applying
Lemmas <REF_0005>
and <REF_0006>.
By
Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma
<REF_0007>
this implies that <MATH_0012> is representable!

<STRUCT_0005><STRUCT_0006>
By
Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma <REF_0008>
it suffices to show that for every scheme <MATH_0013> and morphism <MATH_0014>
the base change <MATH_0015> is an immersion. By
Topologies on Spaces, Lemma <REF_0009>
we can find an fppf covering <MATH_0016> by schemes which refines
the pullback of the covering <MATH_0017> to <MATH_0018>.
Hence we see that <MATH_0019> (which is a morphism of schemes
according to the result of the preceding paragraph) becomes an immersion
after pulling back to the members of an fppf (by schemes) of <MATH_0020>.
Hence <MATH_0021> is an immersion by the result for schemes, see
Descent, Lemma <REF_0010>.
